item.title: Toward Quantum Geospatial Science: What if Geospatial Attributes and Coordinates Are Quantum Entangled?
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 7, November 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACT Spatial modeling traditionally treats geographic coordinates and attributes as separable inputs, introducing spatial dependence through external smoothing, weighting, or graph‐based mechanisms. This paper proposes an alternative representational perspective grounded in quantum theory: what if spatial coordinates and attributes are quantum entangled? Building on the mathematical formalism of Hilbert spaces, superposition, and entanglement, this work conceptualizes coordinate‐feature coupling as structural inseparability rather than as post hoc spatial adjustment. This idea was evaluated using fidelity‐based quantum kernels with varied entanglement topologies. In a Monte Carlo simulation study with analytically defined spatially varying coefficients, coordinate‐feature entanglement consistently improved coefficient recovery relative to equally tuned separable embeddings across multiple regression frameworks, reducing coefficient mean squared error by 9%–12% with SVR and by up to 22% for the best designs, with the largest gains for localized hotspots. Control topologies without coordinate‐feature coupling did not reproduce this gain; the gain emerged only when spatial heterogeneity was strong, and data were sufficient, and no spurious heterogeneity was induced when coefficients were spatially constant. These findings suggest that entanglement functions as a geometric prior that embeds spatial heterogeneity directly within representation rather than introducing it post hoc, offering a principled and extensible direction for quantum‐inspired geospatial modeling.
item.content:encoded:
ABSTRACT

Spatial modeling traditionally treats geographic coordinates and attributes as separable inputs, introducing spatial dependence through external smoothing, weighting, or graph-based mechanisms. This paper proposes an alternative representational perspective grounded in quantum theory: what if spatial coordinates and attributes are quantum entangled? Building on the mathematical formalism of Hilbert spaces, superposition, and entanglement, this work conceptualizes coordinate-feature coupling as structural inseparability rather than as post hoc spatial adjustment. This idea was evaluated using fidelity-based quantum kernels with varied entanglement topologies. In a Monte Carlo simulation study with analytically defined spatially varying coefficients, coordinate-feature entanglement consistently improved coefficient recovery relative to equally tuned separable embeddings across multiple regression frameworks, reducing coefficient mean squared error by 9%–12% with SVR and by up to 22% for the best designs, with the largest gains for localized hotspots. Control topologies without coordinate-feature coupling did not reproduce this gain; the gain emerged only when spatial heterogeneity was strong, and data were sufficient, and no spurious heterogeneity was induced when coefficients were spatially constant. These findings suggest that entanglement functions as a geometric prior that embeds spatial heterogeneity directly within representation rather than introducing it post hoc, offering a principled and extensible direction for quantum-inspired geospatial modeling.
